name: Progress alerts
summary: System-generated conditions that need attention (stalled, slowed down, low confidence, behind or ahead of schedule, potential delay, and support-only types), with snoozing and clearing.

roles.note: The seed catalog has no alert permission strings. Which roles may snooze or clear alerts, or clear them for everyone, is unknown (DEC-005).

nfr.statement: Time from a processed capture to its alerts appearing.
nfr.open_question: Must alerts appear when the capture is published, or within a stated delay?

requirements.title: Which alert types each audience sees
requirements.statement: Every progress project can raise stalled, slowed-down and low-confidence alerts. Takeoff projects add behind, ahead and potential-delay alerts. Support users also see dependency alerts, plus over-100% alerts in takeoff projects. Customers never see the support-only types.

acceptance_criteria.then: Only stalled, slowed-down and low-confidence alerts can appear

acceptance_criteria.given: A takeoff project with a stage over 100%
acceptance_criteria.when: A customer and a support user view alerts
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the support user sees the over-100% alert

requirements.title: Stalled and slowed-down conditions
requirements.statement: A stage is stalled when the latest interval added no progress. It is slowed down when, across the last three captures, the progress per calendar day in the latest interval is lower than in the one before. There is no minimum slowdown percentage.

acceptance_criteria.given: Captures on 1, 8 and 15 March with totals 0, 70 and 70
Captures on 1, 8 and 22 March with totals 0, 70 and 140 (10 per day, then 5 per day)

requirements.title: Behind or ahead of schedule by 15 points
requirements.statement: Schedule variance is the actual percentage minus the scheduled percentage at the latest capture (not today), using the plan end if the capture is later. 15 points or more below is behind, 15 or more above is ahead, and anything between is on track. Completed work has no variance.

acceptance_criteria.given: At the latest capture, 30% is done and 45% was scheduled
acceptance_criteria.then: The stage is behind, because exactly -15 counts as behind

acceptance_criteria.given: At the latest capture, 40% is done and 50% was scheduled

requirements.title: Snoozing is personal and carries to new captures
requirements.statement: A user can snooze an alert for themselves for a number of days or until a date. It ends at the start of that day in the project time zone (America/New_York if unset) and can't run past the project's planned end. When a new capture arrives, an unexpired snooze carries over while the condition persists.

acceptance_criteria.given: User A snoozes a stalled alert for 7 days
acceptance_criteria.then: User B still sees the alert

acceptance_criteria.given: User A's snooze has 5 days left and the stage is still stalled
acceptance_criteria.then: The alert stays snoozed for user A until the original end date

requirements.title: Clearing an alert also suppresses it in future captures
requirements.statement: A manual clear (with a reason, and a comment when the reason is Other) is shared by everyone and removes any personal snoozes for that alert. Today it also hides the same condition in later captures, unlike an automatic clear, which applies to one date only.

dispute.summary: The UI tells users to clear an alert once it is addressed, which suggests one occurrence. The code suppresses the condition in future captures too. Product to decide in DEC-005.

acceptance_criteria.given: A stalled alert manually cleared on 8 March
acceptance_criteria.when: The stage is still stalled at the 15 March capture
acceptance_criteria.then: (Current behaviour) No new stalled alert appears for that stage. Whether it should appear is disputed.
